key_insight: MemFLoRA adapts CNNs at the edge by minimizing activation memory during backpropagation, not just the number of trainable parameters.
engineering_relevance: This makes on-device fine-tuning more feasible for memory-constrained systems such as wearables, sensors, and embedded AI devices.
method: Freezes the down-projection and trains only a scale-matched up-projection.
Uses an activation-memory-floor design so backward computation does not depend on full-width layer inputs.
Combines eval-mode backbone normalization with low-rank, activation-minimal backward rules.
evidence_signal: Across three HAR datasets and two CNN backbones under subject, body-location, and sensor-placement shifts, it cut saved-activation memory by 98.5-98.7% and peak training-state memory by 94.9-97.3% versus full fine-tuning.
watch_item: The approach is tailored to CNN adaptation and its memory savings may depend on implementation details of normalization and backward passes on a given edge framework.
paper_title: MemFLoRA: Memory-Floor LoRA for CNN Adaptation at the Edge
